[P2] Revisit negative context answers that depend on an active lookup

Declare `async function outer(c) { return c.map([1], async inner => inner.map([1], async () => 1)); }` before `withDurableExecution(async (_, ctx) => ctx.runInChildContext(outer))`. The innermost map receives no diagnostic: resolving `c` scans the candidate calls and checks `inner` while `c` temporarily maps to false. That false answer for `inner` is cached permanently, even after `c` is recognized. Consequently, documented nested-context recognition depends on declaration order. Resolve context membership from known roots before reporting, or re-evaluate negatives that depended on unfinished lookups. Add a regression asserting the innermost map is reported with the named function declared before the handler.
